units.text: INT. PIANO RESTORATION WORKSHOP - DAY
A high-ceilinged loft with north light.
Disemboweled pianos stand open on every side, their strings like harps, their hammers laid out on felt cloths in long neat rows.
Sawdust and varnish and old ivory.
NOELLE FAIRCHILD, fifties, the restorer, in a leather apron and reading glasses pushed up into grey curls, bends over a half-dismantled Steinway, a tuning lever in her fist.
DELPHINE ARCHAMBAULT, thirties, her apprentice, stands across the keybed holding a cloth, the curve of her jaw set hard.
LEO FINCH, sixties, the piano's owner, in a rumpled tweed jacket, sits on a bench by the window watching them both, a cane across his knees.
Delphine, the damper felt.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: Which side?
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: The left. The one that's flat.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: Delphine hands her the felt.
She does not let go at once.
Noelle gives it one sharp tug, and Delphine lets go, and neither looks at the other, and Leo studies the dust in the light.
You two have been at this since September.
units.name: LEO

units.text: Fourteen weeks.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: Fifteen.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: It was my wife's piano. She played it every morning for forty years.
units.name: LEO

units.text: I know.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: Delphine knows too. She came to the funeral.
units.name: LEO

units.text: I did.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Noelle sets down the lever.
She straightens slowly, one hand on the small of her back, and looks at Delphine for the first time in the scene.
Delphine meets her gaze and does not blink.
She wanted the middle C re-voiced.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: Who did?
units.name: LEO

units.text: She did. Your wife.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: She told me. She told me last spring, the day I started.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: She told you.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: She didn't want to hurt you.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Leo gets up.
The cane rattles on the floor.
He crosses to the keyboard and presses middle C. A flat, dull note.
Hurt me how?
units.name: LEO

units.text: She said it had been out of tune for years and she played it anyway because you loved it.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Leo presses it again, harder.
The note thuds and dies.
He keeps his finger on the key.
His shoulders bend.
Leo.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: She never said.
units.name: LEO

units.text: She never would.
units.name: NOELLE

units.text: He lifts his hand.
Delphine steps forward as if to touch his arm and stops.
Noelle takes up the tuning lever and sets it against the pin, and nods once at Delphine, and Delphine nods back, and together they begin, slowly, to bring the note home.
